purpose: state how well the system must perform, protect and operate, in measurable terms that design and test can use
entry_criteria: Business and operating context is known
procedure: Cover the main quality areas: performance, availability, security, privacy, usability, maintainability, portability and recoverability.
For each area write a measurable target with the conditions, such as load, data size and time window.
Base the targets on usage forecasts and obligations, and mark each as required or desirable.
Check for conflicts between targets and with cost, and agree the trade-offs with the sponsor.
Say how each will be verified: load test, failover test, audit or review.
Feed the targets to architecture, test planning and monitoring.
deliverables: links to test and monitoring plans
acceptance_criteria: Each target is measurable with its conditions
Targets reach the test and monitoring plans

validation.check: check each non-functional requirement has a number, a condition and a verification method
check each target appears in the test or monitoring plan

failure_modes.detection: Availability target needs more cost than budget

worked_example: ILLUSTRATIVE: Availability of 99.9 percent per month for checkout, recovery within 30 minutes and p95 under 400 ms at 200 requests per second are agreed, each tied to a load or failover test.
